evidence.claim: IEA Electricity 2026 identifies AI, data centers, advanced manufacturing, and broad electrification as important drivers of rising electricity demand.

IEA Energy and AI states that global data-center investment nearly doubled since 2022 and reached about half a trillion dollars in 2024; it also notes that building new transmission lines can take four to eight years in advanced economies and that wait times for critical components such as transformers and cables have doubled in the prior three years.
evidence.source_title: IEA Energy and AI - Executive Summary

evidence.claim: NERC's 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment highlights rising resource-adequacy risks as electricity demand grows from data centers, industrialization, electrification, and DER adoption.
DOE's supply-chain page states that distribution transformer lead times increased from three to six months in 2019 to 12 to 30 months in 2023, driven by supply, labor, and material constraints.
evidence.source_title: DOE Supply Chain and Market Analysis

evidence.claim: DOE reliability materials describe federal efforts to identify at-risk regions and guide interventions as the grid faces explosive load growth from AI and reindustrialization.
Eaton reported first-quarter 2026 record results, with 12-month rolling average order acceleration in Electrical Americas up 42%, driven by data-center momentum.
evidence.source_title: Eaton Reports Record First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: Eaton's Q1 2026 analyst presentation reported total backlog growth of 44% in Electrical Americas and approximately 240% growth in Electrical Americas data-center orders.
evidence.source_title: Eaton First Quarter 2026 Earnings Release / Analyst Presentation

evidence.claim: Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence identifies Powell Industries as a custom-engineered electrical power distribution and control equipment company with exposure to medium-voltage switchgear, integrated power control rooms, e-houses, substations, bus duct, and data-center electrical distribution.

Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence identifies GE Vernova as a reference leader across gas turbines, grid equipment, power conversion, and electrification, useful for benchmarking dispatchable generation and grid equipment scarcity.
Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence identifies Centrus Energy as having potential chokepoint exposure to HALEU and enrichment services needed for advanced reactors and parts of the nuclear fuel chain.

Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence identifies Preformed Line Products as a niche supplier of grid hardware used for transmission, distribution, substation, OPGW/ADSS, and utility infrastructure buildouts.

Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence frames MYR Group as a possible second-order beneficiary if qualified labor, procurement, testing, commissioning, substation construction, and utility interconnect work constrain project timing.

Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence frames IES Holdings as a potential beneficiary if electrical construction labor, systems integration, and project execution become bottlenecks alongside switchgear and transformers.
Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence identifies Vertiv as a reference leader for data-center power and cooling systems, useful for validating AI-related critical infrastructure demand.
Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence identifies Constellation Energy as a reference nuclear power asset with potential value from clean baseload electricity demand and data-center power procurement.
Cached Layer 1 candidate evidence identifies Hubbell as a reference leader for utility grid components, transmission, substation, and grid-modernization demand.

memory_update.text: POWL maps directly to the medium-voltage switchgear, integrated power-control-room, e-house, substation, bus duct, and data-center electrical distribution bottleneck; verify backlog conversion, customer concentration, and execution margin before upgrading.
ETN should remain the reference validation ticker for Electrical Americas backlog, data-center electrical order growth, and electrification demand; do not treat it as underfollowed.

GEV should remain the reference validation ticker for gas-turbine scarcity plus grid equipment demand; use its backlog and lead-time commentary to validate or falsify dispatchable-generation bottlenecks.
LEU maps to the nuclear fuel-cycle/HALEU bottleneck, but evidence must focus on DOE support, licensing, commercial demand, capacity milestones, and funding rather than generic nuclear enthusiasm.
PLPC is a second-order underfollowed grid hardware candidate; the key question is whether substation/HV/EHV and Delta Star-related exposure are material enough to matter.

MYRG and IESC belong in the electrical labor/execution bottleneck lane, but both need backlog and project-mix verification to avoid confusing broad construction cyclicality with AI/grid power infrastructure exposure.

VRT, CEG, and HUBB are reference or semi-reference names used to price the market's view of data-center infrastructure, clean firm power, and utility grid hardware; they should not crowd out smaller supplier discovery.

Need primary-source SEC filings, earnings presentations, transcripts, and investor decks for POWL, PLPC, MYRG, IESC, HUBB, VRT, GEV, LEU, and CEG before Layer 3 scoring; current mapping relies partly on cached Layer 1 evidence.
Need live market-cap, valuation, analyst-coverage, short-interest, and earnings-revision checks to separate true underfollowed candidates from already-consensus winners.

Need falsification tracking for lead-time normalization, backlog cancellations, customer capex digestion, fixed-price contract margin compression, capacity additions, commodity pressure, and regulatory delay.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for the grid/data-center electrical hardware, dispatchable power, nuclear fuel, utility grid components, and electrical execution chunk. The cleanest chokepoint relationships are POWL for medium-voltage switchgear and integrated power control rooms, ETN as the reference validation leader for Electrical Americas/data-center orders, GEV as the reference for grid plus gas-turbine scarcity, LEU for nuclear fuel-cycle/HALEU optionality, PLPC as an underfollowed second-order grid hardware supplier, and MYRG/IESC as labor-and-execution bottleneck hypotheses. Reference leaders are retained for category validation; the underfollowed lane centers on smaller or niche suppliers where public labels may obscure exposure.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether backlog and the large data-center order convert to revenue and margin without capacity, labor, customer-concentration, or fixed-price execution problems.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify latest 10-Q/10-K backlog, segment revenue, gross margin, customer concentration, data-center order detail, capacity expansion, and management commentary on switchgear/power-control-room lead times.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Pure-play-ish public exposure to custom-engineered electrical power distribution and control equipment, including switchgear, integrated power control rooms, e-houses, substations, bus duct, and data-center electrical distribution. In the Serenity map, POWL sits close to the physical bottleneck between large-load demand and energized facilities.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Electrical Americas orders/backlog convert into shipments without margin dilution from capacity ramp, labor, copper/steel costs, or long-cycle execution.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track Electrical Americas orders, backlog, book-to-bill, data-center order growth, capacity additions, decremental/incremental margins, and commentary on project timing.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference leader validating category demand across electrical power distribution, circuit protection, switchgear, busway, data-center electrical orders, utility power distribution, and broader electrification. ETN is not the main underfollowed alpha target but anchors the demand and pricing check for smaller suppliers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether gas-turbine lead times, grid backlog, service margins, and equipment pricing remain tight or normalize as capacity and competitors respond.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify latest GEV backlog by segment, gas power equipment orders, grid orders, turbine slot commentary, service margin trends, and any comments on data-center or utility large-load demand.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference leader for the combined scarcity theme across gas turbines, grid equipment, power conversion, and electrification. Useful for testing whether AI/data-center load growth is pushing utilities and hyperscalers toward dispatchable generation and grid hardware procurement.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether DOE support, contracts, enrichment capacity, licensing, and commercial HALEU demand scale fast enough to support the thesis.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify DOE HALEU awards, NRC/licensing status, enrichment capacity milestones, customer contracts, cash burn, funding needs, and timing mismatch between advanced-reactor demand and commercial revenue.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Potential nuclear fuel-cycle chokepoint tied to enrichment services and HALEU supply needed for advanced reactors and parts of the future nuclear power chain. Relationship is strategically important but more policy- and execution-dependent than near-term electrical equipment demand.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Energy Products, substation hardware, and the Delta Star acquisition materially increase exposure to HV/EHV substation demand versus remaining a small mixed-infrastructure business.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify latest annual report segment/product disclosures, acquisition contribution, utility customer mix, order trends, margin sensitivity to materials, and whether substation/HV hardware is a meaningful revenue driver.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Underfollowed second-order grid hardware supplier with exposure to transmission, distribution, substation connectors, OPGW/ADSS, and utility infrastructure buildouts. The company is one or two steps away from the obvious AI data-center demand driver, making it a candidate for hidden grid capex exposure.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether order growth, backlog conversion, liquid-cooling adoption, and competitive pricing remain strong after hyperscaler capex digestion.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track orders, backlog, hyperscaler/customer concentration, liquid-cooling revenue mix, pricing, lead times, and evidence of competition or normalization in data-center infrastructure.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference leader for data-center power and cooling systems. VRT helps validate whether AI load growth is becoming real orders for critical digital infrastructure, thermal management, UPS, and backup-power-adjacent systems.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether backlog growth is specifically tied to grid modernization, data centers, substations, and large electrical interconnect projects rather than broad construction demand.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify backlog composition, transmission/distribution mix, commercial-and-industrial electrical work, data-center references, labor availability, fixed-price exposure, and margin history during rapid backlog growth.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Second-order beneficiary candidate where qualified electrical labor, procurement, testing, commissioning, substation construction, and utility interconnect work may constrain project timing. The thesis is that execution capacity, not just hardware, becomes a bottleneck.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether nuclear PPA economics, regulatory treatment, capacity-market revenue, uprates, and restart/extension projects justify the market narrative.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify latest PPA disclosures, nuclear fleet output, capacity-market exposure, regulatory treatment, uprate/restart economics, and hyperscaler contract terms where disclosed.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference clean baseload generation asset for testing whether power scarcity is monetized through nuclear PPAs, capacity-market revenue, uprates, restarts, and life-extension economics. Not underfollowed, but important for pricing the value of scarce clean firm power.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center/high-tech work is large enough to matter, whether backlog is power-distribution related, and whether margins are protected under fixed-price contracts.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify segment revenue, backlog if disclosed, customer/project mix, data-center or high-tech facility exposure, fixed-price contract risk, labor constraints, and whether margin expansion is structural or cyclical.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Hypothesis candidate for electrical contracting, infrastructure, and technology systems installation exposure. Potentially benefits if data-center electrical labor, systems integration, and project execution become bottlenecks alongside switchgear and transformers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Utility Solutions growth is broad-based utility capex or concentrated in a few high-growth verticals, and whether pricing/capacity benefits persist.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify Utility Solutions organic growth, backlog/order commentary, substation/transmission exposure, price-cost dynamics, acquisitions, and management comments on grid modernization and data-center-related utility demand.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference-to-semi-reference leader for utility grid components, transmission/distribution hardware, substation products, and grid-modernization demand. Less hidden than PLPC but still useful as a benchmark for smaller grid hardware suppliers.
